sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is doing the business of real estate in Lucknow and due to some dispute with Vivek Kumar Singh Patel, who is the owner/manager of Dr. Ambedkar Higher Secondary School, Daulatyarpur, P.S. Madhoganj.

He further submitted that only with the intention to blackmail the applicant, two complaints were energized, one by Vijay Yadav S/o Banshi, R/o Govind Nagar, Kanpur Nagar dated 9.12.2022 with the allegation that his daughter is working the work of clearing at Dr. Ambedkar Higher Secondary School, Daulatyarpur,
P.S. Madhoganj and on 8.12.2022, applicant came in the premises of the said school, caught her and on the gun point, she was dragged in a room and forcibly raped with life threat.
When he received information then he immediately came to the spot, narrated the incident, and went to the police station but his F.I.R. was not lodged.

He further submitted that on the same date, one application was also given to the Superintendent of Police, Hardoi by Sabina Bano, who is the domestic servant at the house of Vivek Kumar Singh Patel, manager of the aforesaid school and
in the said compliant,
it is alleged that she is a vegetable seller and on the pretext of facilitating the government job, she was being raped by the applicant.

On 7.12.2022 at 6:00 P.M., the applicant sent an unknown person to the victim and told her for making physical relation with the stranger, when she started crying,
then stranger ran away, thereafter, she went to the police station but her F.I.R. was not lodged.

Thereafter, two applications under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. were moved in the Court of A.C.J.M., IV,
Hardoi on 13.12.2021 one by Sabina Bano, another by Vijay Yadav and in both the applications, Mr.
Vivek Mishra, Advocate is the counsel, and under the order of the Court, two F.I.R.s were lodged against the applicant.

Charge sheet has been filed in the F.I.R. No.22/2023, and in the present case,
the investigation is going on.
He further submitted that police is trying to arrest on the behest of aforesaid Vivek Kumar Singh Patel, even applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation.
In such, circumstances, applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant opposed the prayer of the applicant but they do not dispute this fact that two complaints were given to the Superintendent of Police,
Hardoi on 9.12.2022 and thereafter, two applications under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. were moved before the competent court through Mr. Vivek Mishra, Advocate and order was passed for lodging of F.I.R..

They also do not dispute that in F.I.R. No.22/2023, no evidence under Section 376 I.P.C. was found and the charge-sheet was filed for the offence under Section 354-A I.P.C.
6.

Considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and going through the contents of the F.I.R. as well as other relevant documents, it is evident that two complaints were given by two different persons to the Superintendent of Police, Hardoi, thereafter, two applications under Sections 156(3) Cr.P.C. were moved before the competent court through Mr. Vivek Mishra,
Advocate.

As there is a specific avernment of the applicant that the aforesaid both the complaints are related to Mr. Vivek Kumar Sngh Patel, who is inimical with the applicant, therefore, this Court is of the view that no custodial interrogation is necessary, therefore, applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.
7. Thus having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is finally disposed of.

2 crime number is taken into custody, he shall be released on anticipatory bail by the concerned Station House Officer on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount with the following conditions:-
i.
The applicant shall not leave India during the pendency of trial without prior permission from the concerned trial Court.

ii. The applicant shall Cooperate in the investigation and will make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
iii. The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.
iv. The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of any of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law to ensure presence of the applicant.
v. In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail, the trial Court concerned may take appropriate action in accordance with law.

vi. The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and shall proceed against him in accordance with law.
8. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.

9. Superintendent of Police, Hardoi is directed to ensure the fair investigation of the case and also consider each and very aspect provided by the applicant in accordance with the provisions of Section 107 of U.P. Police Regulation Act.
10. Presence of the Officers are hereby discharged.
